first_principles_point: Finance becomes real when it changes what households and businesses can buy, borrow, insure, delay, refinance, or risk.
money_path: household/business need -> bank/card/insurer/payment network/broker/asset manager/private-credit platform -> interest/fee/spread/premium/interchange/advisory economics -> losses/funding/rewards/claims/reserves/capital/liquidity -> durable cash or fragility
company_examples: JPMorgan; American Express; Capital One; Progressive; Visa; Mastercard; Chubb; PayPal; BlackRock; Blackstone
proof_needed: loan balances; deposits; NIM; charge-offs; provisions; payment volume; take rate; premium growth; combined ratio; rewards cost; capital; cash flow
safe_use: Use as a no-background finance frame, not as proof that financial revenue equals clean cash.

first_principles_point: Credit is a bridge across time; losses show when the bridge was too weak.
money_path: need now -> loan/card balance -> interest and fees -> payment behavior -> delinquency/charge-off/reserve -> capital and cash outcome
company_examples: JPMorgan; Capital One; American Express; Synchrony; Affirm
proof_needed: balances; APR/yield; payment rate; delinquency; charge-off; provision; reserve; capital
safe_use: Safe claim: higher loan balances do not prove healthy customers.

old_html_inputs: Membership or Nothing; Affordability Ceiling; Cash Harvest
first_principles_point: Cards are both payment tools and lending products, so spending power and borrower stress must be read together.
money_path: purchase need -> card authorization -> merchant fee/interchange/annual fee/interest -> rewards and funding cost -> delinquency/charge-off/reserve -> earnings/capital
company_examples: American Express; Capital One; JPMorgan; Mastercard; Visa; Synchrony
proof_needed: billed business; purchase volume; receivables; annual fees; rewards cost; delinquencies; charge-offs; reserves
safe_use: Safe claim: card revenue must be read with credit and rewards costs.

first_principles_point: Deposits are a funding product and a liability, not free money for banks.
money_path: customer cash -> bank deposit -> funding base -> loans/securities -> interest income minus deposit cost -> NIM/capital/liquidity
company_examples: JPMorgan; Capital One; regional banks; brokerages
proof_needed: deposit balances; deposit beta; funding cost; liquidity; securities duration; NIM; capital
safe_use: Safe claim: deposit quality depends on cost and stickiness.

first_principles_point: Insurance converts uncertain future loss into a known premium today, but claims and reserves decide whether the price was adequate.
money_path: customer risk -> premium -> insurer float/investment portfolio -> claim/loss adjustment/reserve -> combined ratio and capital
company_examples: Progressive; Chubb; Travelers; Berkshire; MetLife; Prudential
proof_needed: premium growth; loss ratio; combined ratio; claim severity; reserves; investment yield; retention
safe_use: Safe claim: premium growth is not enough without loss and reserve proof.

first_principles_point: Payment networks sell acceptance, authorization, clearing, settlement, fraud control, and trust.
money_path: merchant/customer transaction -> authorization/network/processor -> interchange/service fee/take rate -> fraud/incentive/regulatory cost -> operating margin and cash
company_examples: Visa; Mastercard; PayPal; American Express; Block
proof_needed: payment volume; transactions; cross-border volume; take rate; incentives; fraud; regulation; margin
safe_use: Safe claim: payment volume matters only after take-rate and cost checks.

first_principles_point: A spread is durable only if the route is hard to avoid and losses or funding costs do not eat it.
money_path: mandatory route or balance sheet -> fee/spread/tariff/take rate -> operating cost/loss/funding cost -> durable margin
company_examples: JPMorgan; insurers; brokerages; Visa; Mastercard; private-credit platforms
proof_needed: NIM; fee yield; funding cost; loss cost; route durability; operating margin; capital
safe_use: Safe claim: spreads need route and risk proof.

first_principles_point: Membership finance captures a recurring relationship before each transaction and then stacks fees, rewards, data, and merchant economics on top.
money_path: membership/card account -> recurring fee and higher transaction frequency -> merchant/network economics -> rewards/benefit cost -> retention and lifetime value
company_examples: American Express; Marriott co-brands; JPMorgan cards; Capital One; PayPal
proof_needed: annual fees; card acquisition; fee-paying mix; retention; rewards cost; spend; merchant economics
safe_use: Safe claim: benefits and retention must justify fee growth.

first_principles_point: Finance is the meter that shows whether households are spending from income or borrowed time.
money_path: household budget pressure -> card balance/BNPL/loan demand/insurance shopping/deposit movement -> lender/insurer/payment revenue -> losses/reserves/claims -> cash and capital
company_examples: Capital One; American Express; Affirm; Progressive; PayPal
proof_needed: balances; delinquencies; charge-offs; payment rate; BNPL GMV; insurance shopping; reserve builds
safe_use: Safe claim: spending can look strong before credit quality deteriorates.

first_principles_point: Private platforms route capital, but named-cash proof still requires vehicle schedules, borrower lists, collateral, debt waterfalls, and realization evidence.
money_path: pension/insurance/retail/institutional savings -> asset manager/private vehicle/insurer/BDC -> borrower/asset/project -> interest/rent/fee/exit -> platform fee/spread/cash
company_examples: BlackRock; Blackstone; KKR; Apollo/Athene; Ares; Brookfield; Prudential; MetLife
proof_needed: AUM; FPAUM; inflows; insurance liabilities; dry powder; deployment; realizations; collateral; vehicle schedules
safe_use: Safe claim: AUM is routing scale
column9: not proof of final cash realization.

first_principles_point: Cash returned to shareholders is real, but it must be separated from customer health and productive reinvestment.
money_path: customer fee/spread/premium/payment -> earnings after losses and reserves -> capital allocation -> buybacks/dividends/reinvestment/acquisition/capital buffer
company_examples: American Express; banks; insurers; asset managers; payment networks
proof_needed: buybacks; dividends; capital ratios; reinvestment; technology spend; reserves; customer attrition
safe_use: Safe claim: shareholder return does not prove customer health.

first_principles_point: Finance products often look cheaper than they are because rewards, zero-percent offers, and free services are funded elsewhere.
money_path: visible low price or reward -> hidden funding source -> customer/merchant/platform cost -> retention or loss -> cash effect
company_examples: American Express; Visa; Mastercard; Affirm; PayPal; brokerages
proof_needed: rewards cost; interchange; merchant discount; incentive payments; cash sweep yield; order routing; margin lending
safe_use: Safe claim: ask who funds the reward or free product.

first_principles_point: Credit quality is not proven when a loan is made; it is proven when repayment survives stress.
money_path: loan origination -> interest/fee revenue -> delinquency -> charge-off -> provision/reserve -> capital impact
company_examples: Capital One; JPMorgan; Affirm; Synchrony; American Express
proof_needed: delinquency; charge-off; allowance coverage; provision; vintage performance; payment rate; borrower mix
safe_use: Safe claim: losses are the truth serum for lending growth.

first_principles_point: The balance sheet is part of the product because capital and liquidity determine whether promises survive stress.
money_path: financial promise -> balance-sheet asset/liability mismatch -> stress event -> capital/liquidity response -> survival or forced sale
company_examples: banks; insurers; brokerages; private funds; BDCs
proof_needed: capital ratio; liquidity; duration; redemption terms; collateral calls; reserve adequacy; funding maturity
safe_use: Safe claim: earnings without balance-sheet resilience are incomplete.

first_principles_point: Finance cannot be read with one metric across banks, cards, insurers, payments, brokers, and asset managers.
money_path: company type -> correct financial promise -> correct proof fields -> loss/funding/capital bridge -> cash-quality conclusion
company_examples: JPMorgan; American Express; Capital One; Progressive; Visa; Mastercard; Chubb; PayPal; BlackRock; Blackstone
proof_needed: sector-specific operating metrics plus balance sheet and cash-flow proof
safe_use: Safe claim: read each company by the promise it sells.
